sections.title: Property Sheet — PROP-F (Fiona's house)
sections.md:
| # | Field | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Type and era | 1900s Edwardian stone terrace in a Fife coastal town, kept plain and bright |
| 2 | Shell | sage-green smooth plaster · tall moulded white skirting ~20 cm · moulded white architraves · white four-panel doors, round brass knobs · white ceiling, plaster cornice, glass pendant · stripped pine boards in the hall, oatmeal wool carpet on the stairs, black-and-white quarry tiles in the porch · white cast-iron column radiators · brushed brass switches |
| 3 | Floor map | front door → hall; one straight flight rises away from the door along the **left-hand** wall to a small landing with a window; the front sitting room through the doorway on the **right** |
| 4 | Orientation | the front (door glass, landing window) faces **south**: bright in the morning |
| 5 | Carried elements | the white handrail and square spindles · the oatmeal stair carpet · the coat stand with the red waterproof · the blue glass bowl on the half-moon table |
| 6 | Exterior | grey stone terrace fronts stepping downhill to the sea |
| 7 | Standing negatives | none yet (first plate) |

Alan's house is carried by the kitchen plate: the garden plate attaches it (the back of the house, the kitchen window and white back door are the carried elements). Denise's house appears only in the lounge, so it needs no property plate.

**Light arc (Mode 1, daylight only):** the hooks and the objection lines (HK1, HK2, B2-02) are the only "before" light — Alan's kitchen flat and grey. Everything from the mechanism on is the after: sun in the room, warm, windows bright. Never dark, never moody (§12).
